messages:
maria: heads up, CI deploys to gpu-runtime-prod started failing ~5m ago with 403 when creating pods. pipeline logs show K8s create denied.

raj: can you paste the error?

maria: sure — snippet from deploy job:
```
2024-11-03T18:33:04Z ERROR: pods "inference-worker-xyz" is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:ci:deploy-sa\" cannot create resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"gpu-runtime-prod\"
CausedBy: rbac.authorization.k8s.io: Forbidden
kms: decrypt failed: access denied
```

oliver: interesting, two things: RBAC denied on pods and a KMS decrypt error. Could be the deploy-sa lost namespace-scoped role after the recent role refactor.

ashley: sec-bot just fired an alert about an IAM policy change at 18:30. (sec-bot: change detected: clusterrolebinding deployer-global removed) :warning:

julia: quick mitigation: we can rebind a narrowed role into the namespace while we triage. do NOT re-add the global CRB.

raj: temporary command I ran in my sandbox (DO NOT apply cluster-wide in prod):
```sh
kubectl create rolebinding deploy-pod-creator -n gpu-runtime-prod \ 
  --role=pod-creator-lite --serviceaccount=ci:deploy-sa
```
where pod-creator-lite only allows create/get/list on pods in that ns.

maria: that restored deploys for one pipeline run, thanks. we still have the KMS failures for model Key decrypt in sidecar. error: "kms: access denied for cryptoKeyVersions/decrypt"

oliver: check which SA the sidecar uses. if sidecar uses workload identity mapping to a GCP SA, that mapping might have been rotated or the KMS IAM binding removed in the key policy change.

maria: sidecar uses k8s SA gpu-sidecar-sa -> mapped to cloud service account infra-gpu-sa. I see an IAM change event: removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter from infra-gpu-sa at 18:29.

ashley: likely simultaneous PR that tightened key access and removed a legacy binding. we need two actions: 1) restore minimal KMS decrypt role to infra-gpu-sa, 2) harden RBAC so deploy SA cannot escalate.

julia: proposed long-term fix: split privileges so pipeline has an explicit "namespace-deployer" RoleBinding (namespace-scoped) + a separate "model-kms-access" persona bound only to runtime pods via projected SA token or WorkloadIdentity with key-limited binding. no clusterrole for deploys.

oliver: add audit entries to verify scope of previous change and list principals that had the CRB. Run: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding deployer-global -o yaml` (if gone, check audit logs).

maria: I queried audit logs (GCP) and found the CRB deletion was by user svc-automation@infra.tools at 18:29:12 from CI runner ip. That same automation rotated key bindings. it's a combined pipeline that ran infra-refactor-2024.

raj: next steps I took: 1) re-granted roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to infra-gpu-sa (scoped to single key) 2) applied the namespace-only RoleBinding for deploy-sa 3) created an issue to remove the global CRB permanently and replace with explicit per-namespace bindings.

maria: deploys are green now. leaving this thread to document triage and follow-ups.

ashley: follow-ups list: [ ] revert automation change to only remove CRB after per-namespace rolebindings exist, [ ] add an automated audit gating (check for CRB removal without replacement), [ ] add alert on KMS key principal removals, [ ] run a least-privilege review for all SA that touch GPU pool nodes.

julia: for rollout plan — canary the namespaced bind in staging across 2 namespaces, run a 24h job loadgen, then schedule cluster-wide removal of CRB in maintenance window.

sec-bot: incident-note: gpu-deploy-lockout-2045126789 created. severity: medium. owner: @maria.

raj: pinging infra-oncall to verify no other clusters affected. (raj: :eyes:)

maria: thanks everyone, will create a playbook entry for triage steps (RBAC -> KMS linkage) and assign follow-ups.

oliver: also add a small test in CI that verifies deploy SA can create pods only in allowed ns and cannot in kube-system (quick smoke).

ashley: recorded for runbook. closing once follow-ups are on the board. :white_check_mark:
